author: Shri Raghavendra Swami
commentary: भयङ्करं रूपं किमर्थं दर्शितवानसीत्यतः विश्वरूपदृष्टेर्महिमानमाह भगवान् ॥ सुदुर्दर्शमिति । यन्मम रूपं दृष्टवानसि । अस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणो ये देवाः तेऽपि यद्दृष्टवन्तस्तदिदं सुदुर्दर्शम् । केषाञ्चित्सुखेन दर्शनीयम् । केशाञ्चित्सुखेन दुःखेन च दर्शनीयमित्यर्थः । देवानामप्यपेक्षितत्वात्तव शत्रुवधे निमित्तमात्रत्वज्ञापनाय चैतद्रूपं दर्शितमिति भावः ॥ ११.५२॥
translation:
The blessed Lord said: This form which thou hast beheld, which even the gods are always eager to see (and have also seen), is very hard to see (59.)
V. Sudurdarsa: should be really taken as two words, viz., Sudarsa and Durdarsa meaning delightful to see and fearful and difficult to see. The idea is that for the devotees the sight is not only easily obtained, but also a delightful one. To others it is not only inaccessible, but the source of terror.
Since the sight of this form is sought after even by the gods and it has been necessary to make thee understand that thou art a nominal cause of the coming destruction, I conferred on thee such a vision.
